q: You buy bread at a ___.
explain: A bakery makes and sells bread and cakes. Example: The bakery smells lovely.

q: I feel ___. I need to go to bed.
explain: Tired means you need sleep. Example: I'm tired after football.

notes.thirsty: Thirsty means you need a drink.

q: The opposite of 'cheap' is ___.
explain: Cheap costs little; expensive costs a lot. Example: Diamonds are expensive.

notes.free: Free costs nothing, even less than cheap.
notes.easy: Easy is the opposite of difficult.
notes.heavy: Heavy is the opposite of light.

q: A person who serves food in a restaurant is a ___.
explain: A waiter brings food to your table. Example: The waiter brought our pizza.

notes.chef: A chef cooks the food in the kitchen.

q: Can you ___ me some money? I'll pay you back.
explain: Lend = give for a while. Borrow = take for a while. Example: Can I borrow your pen? / Can you lend me your pen?

notes.borrow: Borrow is what YOU do: Can I borrow some money?
notes.spend: Spend means use money to buy things.
notes.owe: Owe means you must pay someone back.

q: I ___ my homework every evening.
explain: We say do homework. Example: Did you do your homework?

notes.make: We make a cake, but we do homework.
notes.take: Take is for photos or buses.
notes.play: Play is for games and sports.

q: We ___ a photo of the castle.
explain: We take a photo. Example: Take a picture of me!

notes.made: Make a photo isn't natural English.
notes.had: Had a photo means owned one.

q: The train was ___, so we arrived late.
explain: Delayed means later than planned. Example: Our flight was delayed.

notes.early: Early would make you arrive early.
notes.fast: Fast would make you arrive early too.
notes.empty: Empty means no people, not late.

q: Which one is a vegetable?
explain: A carrot is a vegetable. Example: Rabbits love carrots.

q: Put on your ___ — it's raining!
explain: A raincoat keeps you dry. Example: Take your raincoat to school.

q: My mother's brother is my ___.
explain: Your mum's or dad's brother is your uncle. Example: Uncle Ben tells jokes.

notes.cousin: A cousin is your uncle's child.
notes.nephew: A nephew is your brother's or sister's son.
notes.grandfather: A grandfather is your mum's or dad's dad.

q: I'm very ___ in history. I love old castles.
explain: -ed words say how you feel; -ing words describe the thing. Example: I'm interested in this interesting book.

notes.interesting: Interesting describes the thing: History is interesting.
notes.bored: Bored doesn't fit 'I love old castles'.
notes.boring: Boring describes a thing, and doesn't fit.

q: Could you ___ the window? It's hot in here.
explain: Open the window to let air in. Example: Open the door, please.

notes.turn: We turn a key or a tap, not a window.

q: The film was really ___. I laughed a lot.
explain: Funny makes you laugh. Example: a funny clown.

q: A ___ is where you can see old and interesting things.
explain: A museum shows old and interesting things. Example: We saw dinosaur bones at the museum.

notes.stadium: A stadium is for sport and concerts.

q: I need to ___ the bus at the next stop.
explain: Get off = leave a bus or train. Example: Get off at the park.

notes.get on: Get on means go into the bus.
notes.get up: Get up means leave your bed.
notes.get in: Get in is for cars, not buses.

q: Turn ___ the light, please. It's dark.
explain: Turn on = start a light or machine. Example: Turn on the TV.

notes.down: Turn down is for volume or an offer.

q: I'm ___. Can I have a glass of water?
explain: Thirsty means you need a drink. Example: Running makes me thirsty.

notes.angry: Angry is a feeling, not about water.

q: We ___ our holiday in Scotland last year.
explain: We spend time somewhere. Example: I spent the day at the beach.

notes.passed: Passed isn't used with holiday like this.
notes.stayed: Stayed needs 'in': We stayed in Scotland.

q: Don't forget to ___ your teeth before bed.
explain: We brush our teeth. Example: Brush your teeth twice a day.

notes.wash: We wash our hands or face.
notes.clean up: Clean up is for a messy room.

q: The shop ___ at six o'clock, so hurry!
explain: Shops open and close. Example: The bank closes at five.

notes.finishes: A film or lesson finishes, not a shop.
notes.stops: A bus stops; a shop closes.
notes.ends up: End up means arrive somewhere in the end.

q: A ___ is a doctor for animals.
explain: A vet looks after sick animals. Example: We took our cat to the vet.

notes.nurse: A nurse helps doctors with people.

q: I can't find my glasses. Can you help me ___ for them?
explain: Look for = try to find. Example: I'm looking for my keys.

notes.watch: Watch is for TV or games.
notes.find: Find doesn't go with 'for'. Find them.

q: The opposite of 'noisy' is ___.
explain: Noisy and quiet are opposites. Example: Be quiet in the library.

notes.empty: Empty is the opposite of full.
notes.slow: Slow is the opposite of fast.
notes.calm down: Calm down is a verb: Calm down, please.

q: He ___ a cold, so he stayed at home.
explain: We have a cold. Example: I have a cold and a sore throat.

notes.took: We take medicine, not a cold.

q: Which one do you wear on your hands in winter?
explain: Gloves go on your hands. Example: Wear gloves in the snow.

q: Can I ___ on this dress? — Yes, the changing room is there.
explain: Try on = put on clothes to see if they fit. Example: Try on these shoes.

notes.put: Put on is for getting dressed, not testing in a shop.
notes.dress: Dress doesn't go with 'on this dress'.

q: It's very ___ today. Hold on to your hat!
explain: Windy = lots of wind. Example: It's windy, let's fly a kite!

notes.sunny: Sunny wouldn't blow your hat away.
notes.foggy: Foggy means you can't see far.
notes.snowing: Snowing is a verb: It's snowing.

q: My grandma is ___. She's 92!
explain: Elderly is a kind word for old people. Example: an elderly neighbour.

notes.modern: Modern is for things, not people's age.
notes.early: Early is about time, not age.

q: Please ___ the form and give it back to me.
explain: Fill in a form = write the answers. Example: Fill in your name.

notes.fill up: Fill up is for a glass or a car's tank.
notes.write on: Write on a form isn't how we say it.

q: I'd like to ___ a table for two at eight.
explain: Book a table = reserve it. Example: We booked a table for Gran's birthday.

notes.order: Order is for food: I'd like to order pizza.
notes.buy: You can't buy a restaurant table!

q: You borrow books from a ___.
explain: A library lends books for free; a bookshop sells them.

notes.bookshop: A bookshop sells books; you don't borrow them.

q: You buy medicine at a ___.
explain: A pharmacy (chemist's) sells medicine.

q: You send a parcel at the ___.
explain: You post letters and parcels at the post office.

notes.police station: The police station is for the police.

q: We watched the football match at the ___.
explain: A stadium is a big place for sport and concerts.

notes.library: A library is quiet, for books.
notes.hospital: A hospital is for sick people.

q: Our plane leaves from the ___ at six.
explain: Planes use an airport.

notes.bus stop: Buses stop at a bus stop.

q: I'm ___ of the dark. Can you leave the light on?
explain: Feelings: scared (of) = afraid.

notes.bored: Bored means nothing interesting is happening.
notes.proud: Proud is a good feeling about something you did.

q: I got 100% in the test! I feel so ___.
explain: Proud = pleased about something you did.

notes.nervous: Nervous is how you feel before the test.
notes.lonely: Lonely means you're alone and sad.

q: I have nothing to do. I'm so ___.
explain: -ed adjectives = how you feel; -ing = what something is like.

notes.boring: Boring describes the thing, not your feeling.
notes.busy: Busy means you have lots to do.
notes.excited: Excited means looking forward to something.

q: The film was so ___ that I fell asleep.
explain: -ing adjective describes the film.

notes.exciting: An exciting film keeps you awake.
notes.frightened: Frightened is how a person feels.

q: Tomorrow is my birthday! I'm really ___.
explain: Excited = happy because something good is coming.

notes.exciting: Exciting describes the thing (an exciting party).
notes.worried: Worried means you think something bad may happen.

q: I'm ___ about the test. I hope I pass.
explain: Nervous = a bit worried before something.

notes.proud: Proud comes after you do well.

q: Please ___ your shoes before you come in.
explain: Phrasal verbs: take off clothes/shoes = remove them.

notes.get up: Get up means leave your bed.
notes.turn off: Turn off is for machines and lights.

q: I ___ at seven o'clock every morning.
explain: Get up = get out of bed.

notes.get on: Get on is for buses and trains.
notes.look after: Look after means take care of.

q: Can you ___ my cat while I'm away?
explain: Look after = take care of.

notes.look for: Look for means try to find.
notes.look at: Look at means turn your eyes to.
notes.look like: Look like means seem similar to.

q: Don't ___! You can do it!
explain: Give up = stop trying.

notes.get up: Get up means out of bed.

q: Please ___ your toys and put them in the box.
explain: Pick up = lift from the floor.

notes.go out: Go out means leave the house.

q: I'll ___ the music. It's too loud.
explain: Turn down = make quieter.

notes.turn around: Turn around means face the other way.

q: The opposite of 'early' is ___.
explain: Opposites: early ↔ late.

notes.soon: Soon means in a short time.

q: The opposite of 'heavy' is ___.
explain: Opposites: heavy ↔ light (weight).

notes.soft: Soft is the opposite of hard.
notes.thin: Thin is the opposite of thick or fat.
notes.easy: Easy is the opposite of difficult.

q: The opposite of 'difficult' is ___.
explain: Opposites: difficult ↔ easy.

notes.simple-minded: Simple-minded is about people, and unkind.

q: The opposite of 'wet' is ___.
explain: Opposites: wet ↔ dry.

notes.cold: Cold is the opposite of hot.
notes.clean: Clean is the opposite of dirty.

q: The opposite of 'win' is ___.
explain: Opposites: win ↔ lose a game.

notes.fail: Fail is for tests, not games.
notes.miss: Miss means not hit or not catch.

q: The opposite of 'remember' is ___.
explain: Opposites: remember ↔ forget.

q: Can you ___ me to feed the fish?
explain: Remind someone to do something = help them remember.

notes.remember: Remember is what you do yourself.

q: Please ___ me how to play this game.
explain: Show someone how to do something.

notes.see: See is what your eyes do.

q: Can you ___ me a story?
explain: Tell + person + a story/joke.

notes.say: Say doesn't take a person directly.
notes.speak: Speak is about languages or talking.

q: I always ___ my bed in the morning.
explain: Collocation: make your bed.

notes.do: We say do homework, not do your bed.
notes.get: Get doesn't go with bed here.

q: Let's ___ a picnic in the park!
explain: Collocation: have a picnic / have a party.

notes.make: Make a picnic means prepare the food, but we say have a picnic.

q: We ___ a lot of fun at the fair.
explain: Collocation: have fun.

notes.made: We don't say make fun here; make fun of is unkind.

q: Don't ___ a noise! The baby is asleep.
explain: Collocation: make a noise.

notes.do: We don't say do a noise.

q: Let's ___ the washing-up together.
explain: Collocation: do the washing-up / do homework.

q: Smile! I'm going to ___ a photo.
explain: Collocation: take a photo.

notes.make: We don't say make a photo in English.
notes.draw: You draw a picture, not a photo.

q: A ___ is a small river.
explain: Nature: a stream is a small river.

notes.lake: A lake is water with land all around.
notes.ocean: An ocean is a huge sea.
notes.hill: A hill is a small mountain.

q: A ___ is a very high hill.
explain: A mountain is very high.

notes.valley: A valley is low land between hills.
notes.island: An island has water all around it.
notes.field: A field is flat land with grass.

q: Land with water all around it is an ___.
explain: An island is surrounded by water.

notes.ocean: An ocean is the water itself.
notes.desert: A desert is dry and sandy.

q: A ___ is very dry and sandy, with almost no rain.
explain: Desert (one s) = dry land; dessert (two s) = sweet food.

notes.jungle: A jungle is wet and green.
notes.beach: A beach is next to the sea.

q: After dinner we had ice cream for ___.
explain: Dessert = the sweet course at the end.

q: A ___ is a hot, wet forest with lots of animals.
explain: A jungle (rainforest) is hot and wet.

notes.village: A village is a small town.

q: Please ___ the plants. They look thirsty.
explain: Water (verb) = give water to plants.

notes.pour: Pour needs an object: pour water on.

q: I'll ___ the table for dinner.
explain: Collocation: set/lay the table.

notes.put: Put needs a thing and a place.
notes.make: Make the table means build it.

q: I'm saving my pocket ___ to buy a game.
explain: Pocket money = money parents give children.

notes.coin: Coin is one piece of money.
notes.price: A price is how much something costs.

q: How much does this toy ___?
explain: How much does it cost? asks the price.

q: I ___ all my money on sweets!
explain: Spend money on something.

notes.paid: Pay needs for: paid for sweets.
notes.cost: Cost is for the thing: the sweets cost £2.
notes.bought: Bought needs the thing directly, not money on.

q: The ___ of this book is £5.
explain: Price = how much something costs.

notes.prize: A prize is something you win.
notes.money: Money is what you pay with.
notes.bill: A bill is the paper that tells you what to pay.

q: She won first ___ in the drawing competition.
explain: Prize = something you win.

notes.price: Price is how much something costs.
notes.place-card: A place-card shows where to sit.
notes.score: Score is the points; you win a prize.

q: Turn ___ at the traffic lights.
explain: Directions: turn left / turn right.

notes.lift: A lift takes you up and down.

q: Go ___ on, then turn right.
explain: Go straight on = don't turn.

q: The café is ___ the bank. You can see it across the road.
explain: Opposite = on the other side of the road.

notes.behind of: We say behind, not behind of.

q: I ___ my keys. I can't find them anywhere!
explain: Lose = can't find something any more. Example: I've lost my pencil.

notes.have missed: Miss is for buses or people you want to see.
notes.have found: Found is the opposite: you have them again.
notes.have kept: Kept means you still have them.

q: Hurry, or we'll ___ the bus!
explain: Miss the bus = be too late for it.

q: A ___ is a book of words and their meanings.
explain: A dictionary explains words.

notes.diary: A diary is where you write your day.
notes.comic: A comic tells a story in pictures.

q: I write about my day in my ___.
explain: Diary = your personal daily book.

notes.dairy: Dairy is milk and cheese (spelling trap!).

q: At a restaurant, you look at the ___ to choose food.
explain: A menu shows the food you can order.

notes.recipe: A recipe tells you how to cook.
notes.list: A list is any set of things.

q: I need flour, eggs and milk. Let's read the ___.
explain: A recipe tells you how to cook something.

notes.receipt: A receipt is the paper after you pay.
notes.menu: A menu is in a restaurant.

q: Keep your ___ in case you want to return the toy.
explain: Receipt = the paper that shows you paid.

q: You need a ___ to get on the train.
explain: A ticket lets you travel or go in.

notes.passport: A passport is for other countries.
notes.stamp: A stamp goes on a letter.

q: My little brother has a ___. He's got a high temperature.
explain: Fever = a high temperature.

notes.cough: A cough is a noise from your throat.
notes.headache: A headache is pain in your head.
notes.toothache: Toothache is pain in your tooth.

q: I ate too much cake. Now I have a ___.
explain: Too much food → stomach ache.

notes.sore throat: A sore throat hurts when you swallow.

q: A ___ is a person who writes books.
explain: Jobs from verbs: write → writer.

q: A ___ works on a farm.
explain: A farmer works on a farm.

q: A ___ fixes cars.
explain: A mechanic repairs cars.

q: A ___ looks after your teeth.
explain: A dentist checks and fixes teeth.

q: It's ___ outside. I can't see the trees.
explain: Foggy = thick cloud near the ground.

q: There was a big ___ with thunder and lightning.
explain: A storm has strong wind, rain and thunder.

notes.breeze: A breeze is a light wind.
notes.shower: A shower is short, light rain.

q: The ___ will tell us if it will rain tomorrow.
explain: Weather forecast = what the weather will be.

notes.weather map: A weather map only shows the weather, it doesn't tell you.
notes.news story: A news story is about events.

q: I keep my clothes in a ___.
explain: A wardrobe is a tall cupboard for clothes.

notes.cupboard in the kitchen: Kitchen cupboards hold food and plates.

q: Put the milk back in the ___.
explain: A fridge keeps food cold.

notes.sink: A sink is for washing up.
notes.drawer: A drawer is for small things.

q: Bake the cake in the ___ for 30 minutes.
explain: You bake in an oven.

q: Our class went on a school ___ to the zoo.
explain: A school trip = a short visit with your class.

notes.travel: Travel is a verb or uncountable noun.
notes.journey home: A journey home is going back.
notes.holiday: A holiday is time off school.

q: We need to ___ our bags for the holiday.
explain: Pack = put things in a bag for a trip.

notes.fill up: Fill up is for petrol or a glass.
notes.load: Load is for lorries and machines.

q: Let's ___ a tent by the lake.
explain: Put up a tent = build it.

notes.set off: Set off means start a journey.

q: We ___ very early to catch the train.
explain: Set off = start a journey.

q: The plane will ___ in five minutes.
explain: A plane takes off when it leaves the ground.

notes.set off: People set off; planes take off.

q: A ___ carries letters to your house.
explain: A postman (post carrier) brings letters.

q: I'm going to ___ for the swimming team.
explain: Try out for a team = do a test to join.

notes.work out: Work out means exercise or solve.

q: Can you ___ what time the film starts?
explain: Find out = discover information.

notes.look after: Look after means take care of.

q: I can't ___ this sum. Can you help?
explain: Work out = solve.

notes.take off: Take off is for clothes or planes.

q: Let's ___ a story about a pirate cat!
explain: Make up = invent.

notes.make out: Make out means see with difficulty.
notes.look up: Look up is for a dictionary.

q: If you don't know a word, ___ it ___ in the dictionary.
explain: Look a word up = find it in a dictionary.

notes.look … for: Look for means search for something lost.
notes.look … after: Look after means take care of.
notes.look … at: Look at means turn your eyes to.

q: She's very ___. She always shares her sweets.
explain: Generous = happy to give and share.

notes.lazy: Lazy means doesn't want to work.
notes.shy: Shy means nervous with new people.

q: He's ___. He doesn't like talking to new people.
explain: Shy = quiet and nervous with people you don't know.

notes.brave: Brave means not afraid of danger.

q: Spell the word: a place where you borrow books
explain: li-brar-y: library.

q: Spell the word: the day after Monday
explain: Tuesday (u-e-s).

q: Spell the word: you wear them on your eyes to see better
explain: glasses: double s.

q: Spell the word: a doctor for animals
explain: vet.

q: Spell the word: the opposite of 'cheap'
explain: ex-pen-sive.

q: Spell the word: the meal in the middle of the day
explain: lunch.

q: Spell the word: a very big, grey animal with a long nose
explain: el-e-phant: ph says f.

q: Spell the word: the season after spring
explain: summer: double m.

q: Spell the word: a person who looks after your teeth
explain: A dentist checks and cleans your teeth.

q: Spell the word: the room where you cook
explain: We cook food in the kitchen.

q: Spell the word: a big group of trees
explain: A forest has lots and lots of trees.

q: Spell the word: the opposite of cheap
explain: Cheap costs a little; expensive costs a lot.

q: Spell the word: you use it to take photos
explain: A camera takes photos.

q: Spell the word: the day before today
explain: Today, yesterday, tomorrow: yesterday was the day before today.

q: Spell the word: a place where you see animals from all over the world
explain: At the zoo you can see lions, monkeys and penguins.

q: Spell the word: a person who flies a plane
explain: A pilot flies a plane.

q: Spell the word: the season after winter
explain: Winter, spring, summer, autumn: spring comes after winter.

q: Spell the word: you put it on your head when it is cold
explain: A hat keeps your head warm.

q: Spell the word: very, very good
explain: Excellent means very, very good.

q: Spell the word: a short sleep in the day
explain: Babies often have a nap after lunch.

q: Spell the word: a ticket to fly somewhere, and the trip itself
explain: Our flight to Spain took two hours.

q: Spell the word: the opposite of borrow: you give something for a short time
explain: I lend you my pen; you borrow my pen.

q: Spell the word: an animal with a long neck
explain: Giraffes have very long necks.

q: Spell the word: a person who cuts your hair
explain: The hairdresser gave me a short summer haircut.

q: Spell the word: not dangerous
explain: Safe means nothing bad will happen.

q: Spell the word: the number after nineteen
explain: Nineteen, twenty, twenty-one.

q: Spell the word: you wear it on your wrist to know the time
explain: A watch shows the time on your wrist.

q: Spell the word: the feeling when you want to drink
explain: When you are thirsty, you want a drink.

q: Spell the word: a meal outside on a blanket
explain: We had a picnic in the park with sandwiches.

q: Spell the word: a place to swim indoors
explain: A swimming pool is a place to swim.

q: Spell the word: very tired
explain: After the long race we were exhausted.

q: Spell the word: not loud
explain: Please be quiet in the library.

q: Spell the word: the person who brings letters
explain: The postman brings letters to our house.

q: Spell the word: the opposite of win
explain: Win and lose are opposites.

q: Spell the word: a sweet food made on your birthday
explain: We eat birthday cake with candles.

q: Spell the word: something you find funny makes you do this
explain: A funny joke makes you laugh.

q: Spell the word: the place where planes take off
explain: Planes take off and land at the airport.

q: Spell the word: twelve o'clock in the daytime
explain: Midday is twelve o'clock in the daytime, around lunchtime.

q: Which picture shows that someone is very sleepy?
options: a face laughing with its eyes shut
a boy in a chef's hat
explain: Zzz is the sound of someone asleep, so it shows a very tired, sleepy person.

notes.a boy running fast: This boy is running fast. He has lots of energy, so he isn't sleepy.
notes.a face laughing with its eyes shut: This face is laughing at something funny. It is wide awake.
notes.a boy in a chef's hat: This boy is ready to cook dinner, not ready for bed.

q: Which picture shows someone who is worried?
options: a boy with a frown and wobbly mouth
a round face with rosy cheeks
a child sitting cross-legged, eyes closed
a face with little hearts around it
explain: When you are worried, you think something bad might happen, so your face frowns a little.

notes.a round face with rosy cheeks: This face is smiling happily, so it isn't worried.
notes.a child sitting cross-legged, eyes close: This child is sitting quietly and feels calm and peaceful.
notes.a face with little hearts around it: The hearts show this face loves something. It feels happy, not worried.

q: It's very cold and snowy today. Who is dressed for the weather?
options: a hero in a fluffy blue coat
a boy in a T-shirt and shorts
a mermaid with a shiny tail
a girl in a red silk dress
explain: A thick, fluffy coat keeps you warm in the snow.

notes.a boy in a T-shirt and shorts: A T-shirt and shorts are for hot, sunny days. He would be very cold!
notes.a mermaid with a shiny tail: A mermaid lives in the sea. She isn't wearing warm clothes for snow.
notes.a girl in a red silk dress: A thin silk dress is pretty, but it won't keep you warm in the snow.

q: You are lost in a big forest. Which one helps you find the way?
explain: A map shows the paths and places, so you can find your way.

notes.an hourglass with sand: An hourglass shows how much time has passed. It can't show you the way.
notes.a little purple teapot: A teapot makes tea. It doesn't help you find the path.
notes.a calendar page: A calendar shows the days and months, not the paths in a forest.

q: Where can you sleep when you go camping?
options: a little shop with a heart
explain: When you camp, you sleep outside in a tent.

notes.a building with tall columns: That's a museum. You visit it in the day to see old things.
notes.a little shop with a heart: That's a shop. You buy things there, but you don't sleep there.
notes.a yellow school bus: That's a school bus. It takes you to school, not camping.

q: Who cooks food in a restaurant kitchen?
options: a boy in a tall white hat
a boy in shiny armour with a sword
a child in a white space suit
a girl dancing in a dress
explain: A chef wears a tall white hat and cooks food in a kitchen.

notes.a boy in shiny armour with a sword: A knight fights dragons in stories. He doesn't cook in a restaurant.
notes.a child in a white space suit: An astronaut flies into space, not into a kitchen.
notes.a girl dancing in a dress: A dancer dances on a stage. She doesn't cook the food.

q: Which pet is wearing glasses?
options: a purple owl holding a book
explain: Look at the eyes: the owl has round glasses on, like someone who loves reading.

notes.an orange fox: Look at the fox's eyes. There are no glasses on its face.
notes.a black and white panda: The panda has black patches round its eyes, but no glasses.
notes.a grey penguin: The penguin has big eyes, but it isn't wearing glasses.

q: Which picture shows rainy weather?
options: a grey cloud with drops falling
a sun peeping out from a cloud
explain: Rain falls from grey clouds in drops of water.

notes.a sun peeping out from a cloud: The sun is coming out, so the weather is getting brighter, not rainy.
notes.a rainbow between two clouds: A rainbow comes after the rain, when the sun shines again.
notes.a smiling yellow sun: A bright sun means a sunny day. You won't need an umbrella.

q: Which one keeps your feet warm in winter?
explain: You wear socks on your feet, and they keep your toes warm.

notes.a pink cap: You wear a cap on your head, not on your feet.
notes.heart-shaped sunglasses: Sunglasses go on your eyes when it's sunny.
notes.a blue bow tie: A bow tie goes round your neck to look smart.

q: Which one is a vegetable?
explain: A carrot is a vegetable. It grows under the ground.

notes.a yellow banana: A banana is a fruit. It grows on a tree.
notes.a bunch of grapes: Grapes are fruit. They grow in bunches.

q: In this sport, you hit a shuttlecock over a high net. Which one?
options: a long racket and a white shuttle
an orange ball with black lines
explain: Badminton is played with a light racket and a feathery shuttlecock.

notes.an orange ball with black lines: That's a basketball. You throw it into a hoop.
notes.a black and white ball: That's a football. You kick it into a goal.
notes.a fuzzy green ball: That's a tennis ball. Tennis has a net too, but you hit a ball, not a shuttlecock.

q: Which one tells you exactly how long a race took?
explain: You press a stopwatch at the start and the end of a race to see how many seconds it took.

notes.a calendar page: A calendar shows days, not the seconds of a race.
notes.a gold medal: You win a medal at the end of a race, but it doesn't tell the time.
notes.a pink megaphone: A megaphone makes your voice loud, but it doesn't time the race.

q: Which hero is ready to sail the sea to look for treasure?
options: a girl in a striped top and long blue coat
a boy in shiny armour with a sword
a boy in a green vest with a bag
a girl in a pink apron with a whisk
explain: A pirate sails a ship and follows a treasure map. Look at her map and sailor's coat.

notes.a boy in shiny armour with a sword: A knight rides a horse and fights with a sword. He doesn't sail ships.
notes.a boy in a green vest with a bag: This explorer walks in the forest, not across the sea.
notes.a girl in a pink apron with a whisk: This girl is ready to bake cakes, not to sail a ship.
